1	# Spec: Claude Code Background Sessions in the Control Room
2	
3	Status: design spec, ready for implementation planning. Builds on
4	`docs/scope.md` (CLI investigation + chosen approach) and
5	`docs/challenge.md` (adversarial review of that approach). This document is
6	the synthesis: every challenge point is adjudicated explicitly in §4, and the
7	adjudication changes the design in §1–§3 rather than sitting beside it.
8	
9	## 0. What this feature is, in one paragraph
10	
11	The Control Room already surfaces OpenCode's native sessions through
12	`admin/opencode_client.py` (HTTP) and `scripts/supervise.py` (a separate
13	poll-and-relay process). Claude Code has no HTTP API for background
14	sessions — the `claude` CLI itself is the only documented contract
15	(`claude --bg`, `claude agents --json --all`, `claude logs`, `claude stop`/
16	`kill`, `claude respawn`, `claude rm`, `claude daemon status`/`stop`). This
17	feature adds a parallel fleet section, "Claude background sessions," that
18	lists those sessions, relays their output into the Control Room's existing
19	SSE transport, and offers a narrow, confirmed set of lifecycle controls —
20	without inventing any steering capability the CLI doesn't document.
21	
22	## 1. Design overview
23	
24	### 1.1 Scope of this phase
25	
26	In scope: **observe** (roster, per-session transcript tail, daemon status)
27	and **lifecycle control** (start, stop/kill, respawn, rm, daemon stop) for
28	`claude --bg` sessions, reusing the Control Room's existing card/transcript
29	UI and SSE plumbing.
30	
31	Out of scope, explicitly: an AI health-flagging monitor analogous to
32	`scripts/supervise.py`'s flash-model "healthy / stalled / off_track"
33	assessment loop over OpenCode sessions. `docs/scope.md`'s Problem section
34	motivates this feature by naming both halves of the OpenCode surface —
35	observe/control (`opencode_client.py`) *and* flagging (`supervise.py`) — but
36	the Chosen Integration Approach only builds the first half. §4.4 records this
37	as a deliberate phasing decision, not an oversight: `claude logs <id>`
38	output is exactly the kind of text `supervise_once`'s batching already knows
39	how to summarize, so a Claude-session flagging monitor is a real, buildable
40	follow-on once this phase's log relay exists to feed it — just not part of
41	this delivery.
42	
43	### 1.2 Session ownership: the central design decision
44	
45	Claude Code's `claude agents --json --all` lists **every** background
46	session the local `claude daemon` supervisor hosts, including ones an
47	operator started by hand in an unrelated terminal — the CLI has no concept
48	of "sessions this UI started." Left unaddressed, that means the Control
49	Room would render Stop/Respawn/Rm buttons on sessions it has no relationship
50	to. This spec resolves that (§4.1) by splitting every session the roster
51	returns into two classes:
52	
53	- **Owned** — started via this feature's `POST /api/claude-agents`. Recorded
54	  in a Redis set (`claude_bg:owned_sessions`) at start time. Gets full
55	  lifecycle control, a continuously relayed transcript from launch, and the
56	  full card treatment.
57	- **External** — present in `claude agents --json --all` but not in the
58	  owned set. Gets a roster row with an "external — not started here" badge,
59	  a one-shot best-effort log fetch, and **no** lifecycle control affordance
60	  — Stop/Respawn/Rm are not rendered, and the corresponding endpoints reject
61	  the action server-side (not just client-side) if the id isn't owned.
62	
63	This mirrors the reasoning `docs/scope.md` already applies to `claude daemon
64	stop` ("affects every session the supervisor hosts, not just ones started
65	from the Control Room") and extends it to the plain roster list, which the
66	original scope left unscoped.
67	
68	### 1.3 Fleet layout
69	
70	The existing fleet view (`admin/static/app.js`, cell cards + design-session
71	cards) gains one additive section, "Claude background sessions," rendered
72	with the same card list markup and selection pattern `selectCell`/
73	`selectDesignSession` already use [admin/static/app.js:721-801]. No new
74	page, panel type, or visual language.
75	
76	Each card shows: session id (truncated with full id on hover/title attr),
77	status (`running`/`stopped`/`completed`/`unknown`, taken from the roster
78	JSON), task/title (truncated), model, cwd, started/updated timestamps, and
79	an **Owned**/**External** badge per §1.2. Owned cards render Stop, Respawn,
80	Rm, and Detach controls in a control panel below the transcript pane,
81	mirroring the existing Interrupt/Detach panel for design sessions
82	[admin/static/app.js:1267-1304] minus Interrupt (§3.4 explains why no
83	interrupt-equivalent exists) plus Respawn and Rm. External cards render only
84	Detach and a "fetch latest log tail" button.
85	
86	A separate, always-visible **Daemon** panel (not per-card) shows `claude
87	daemon status` output read-only, plus a single, separately gated "Stop
88	daemon" control (§3.5).
89	
90	### 1.4 Session id → renderable identity
91	
92	A background session's CLI-native id becomes the Control Room's `cell_id`
93	for that session, namespaced as `claude_bg_<id>`, the same trick
94	`scripts/supervise.py`'s `_cell_id_for` already uses for OpenCode sessions
95	[scripts/supervise.py:151-155]. Concretely:
96	
97	- The id is validated against a strict allowlist pattern
98	  (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`) everywhere it crosses a trust boundary — reading
99	  it from `claude agents --json` output, accepting it as a URL path segment,
100	  and using it to build a Redis key or `LivePublisher` cell id. An id that
101	  fails the pattern is dropped from the roster with a logged warning rather
102	  than passed through; this is the same discipline `_slugify` applies to
103	  OpenCode titles/models before building a `cell_id`
104	  [scripts/supervise.py:146-155], made stricter here because a background
105	  session id (unlike a free-text title) is expected to already be a stable
106	  machine identifier and any deviation is more likely an attack or a parsing
107	  bug than legitimate data.
108	- `GET /api/events/claude_bg_<id>` is the existing, unmodified
109	  `/api/events/<cell_id>` endpoint [admin/server.py:450-490] — no new SSE
110	  route, no new frontend `EventSource` handling. The frontend's
111	  `selectClaudeAgent(id, attach)` (new, mirroring `selectDesignSession`
112	  [admin/static/app.js:758-801]) just points `state.selectedId` at
113	  `claude_bg_<id>` and calls the existing `connectSelectedStream()`.
114	- The roster entry the browser renders and the `cell_id` used for its
115	  transcript are thus always derivable from each other by one string
116	  operation (`claude_bg_` + id / strip the prefix), so no separate id-mapping
117	  table is needed anywhere in the stack.
118	
119	## 2. Observe path + endpoint contract
120	
121	### 2.1 Why polling moves out of the Flask process
122	
123	`admin/server.py`'s own docstring already flags that `app.run(threaded=True)`
124	is a single-process dev server where every SSE client holds one request
125	thread for the life of a tab [admin/server.py:16-20]. Adding a module-level
126	thread that shells out to `claude agents --json --all` on an interval, plus
127	one polling thread per relayed session, stacks more long-lived
128	thread-plus-blocking-subprocess load onto that same process. §4.3 adopts the
129	challenge's alternative: give Claude-agent polling the same treatment
130	`scripts/supervise.py` already gets for OpenCode — a separate process that
131	owns every polling `subprocess` call and writes only to Redis, with
132	`admin/server.py` staying a Redis reader for the roster/transcript paths.
133	Mutating actions (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon status/stop) are short,
134	bounded, one-shot commands and stay as synchronous subprocess calls inside
135	Flask request handlers — it is specifically continuous polling, not all
136	subprocess use, that doesn't belong in the request-serving process.
137	
138	### 2.2 `admin/claude_agents_client.py`
139	
140	A subprocess wrapper mirroring the shape of `OpenCodeClient`
141	[admin/opencode_client.py] but calling the `claude` CLI instead of an HTTP
142	API, following the same binary-resolution and subprocess pattern
143	`claude_adapter.py` already uses for headless runs
144	[src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:36-46, 291-299]:
145	
146	```
147	list_agents(cwd: str, *, all: bool = True, timeout: float = 15.0) -> list[dict]
148	    # claude agents --json [--all] --cwd <cwd>
149	start_agent(task: str, *, cwd: str, model: str, advisor: str | None,
150	            skip_permissions: bool, timeout: float = 15.0) -> dict
151	    # claude --bg "<task>" --cwd <cwd> [--model <model>] [--advisor <advisor>]
152	    #   [--dangerously-skip-permissions]
153	get_logs(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> str
154	    # claude logs <session_id>
155	stop_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
156	    # claude stop <session_id>
157	respawn_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
158	    # claude respawn <session_id>
159	rm_agent(session_id: str, *, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
160	    # claude rm <session_id>
161	daemon_status(*, timeout: float = 5.0) -> dict
162	    # claude daemon status  (exit code 1 => {"running": False})
163	daemon_stop(*, keep_workers: bool = True, timeout: float = 10.0) -> dict
164	    # claude daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]
165	```
166	
167	Every call returns parsed JSON (or, for `get_logs`, raw text) on success and
168	raises a `ClaudeAgentsError` (mirroring `OpenCodeError`
169	[admin/opencode_client.py:28-36]) that distinguishes: binary not found,
170	non-zero exit (with captured stderr), malformed JSON, and timeout. No call
171	touches stdin — every subprocess is invoked with `stdin=DEVNULL` so a
172	misbehaving command can never block waiting for terminal input, which is the
173	concrete risk the scope already flags for `attach`/`agents` (§ "What is
174	explicitly NOT possible").
175	
176	### 2.3 `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py`
177	
178	A new, separate long-running process, structurally parallel to
179	`scripts/supervise.py` but simpler (no monitor-session flagging loop — that's
180	explicitly deferred, §1.1):
181	
182	- **Roster refresh.** Every `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds (default
183	  10), for each path in the configured workdir allowlist (§3.2), runs
184	  `list_agents(path, all=True)`. Unions the results by id (a session can only
185	  be under one cwd, so this is a simple dict merge), tags each entry
186	  `owned: <id in claude_bg:owned_sessions>`, and writes the resulting JSON
187	  array to a Redis key `claude_bg:roster` with a TTL of `2 *
188	  CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds. The TTL means a dead/stalled
189	  supervisor produces a visibly stale (then absent) roster rather than a
190	  silently frozen one.
191	- **Transcript relay — owned sessions only.** For every roster entry with
192	  `owned: true` and a non-terminal status (or a terminal status reached less
193	  than `CLAUDE_AGENTS_RELAY_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 120, ago — so the final
194	  lines of a just-finished session are still captured), the supervisor
195	  ensures one relay thread is running, mirroring `_relay_session`
196	  [scripts/supervise.py:158-176]: loop, call `get_logs(id)`, diff against a
197	  per-session cursor (line count) stored in Redis
198	  (`claude_bg:cursor:<id>`), publish only the new lines through
199	  `LivePublisher(f"claude_bg_{id}")` [src/instrument/live.py:47-105], sleep,
200	  repeat. The thread exits once the grace period after a terminal status
201	  elapses, and `LivePublisher.set_status("done")` is called so the frontend's
202	  existing "stream ended" handling applies unchanged.
203	- **No relay for external sessions.** Sessions present in the roster but not
204	  in `claude_bg:owned_sessions` are never polled for logs by the supervisor.
205	  This is both the resource bound the challenge asked for (§4.3) and a
206	  courtesy/safety boundary: the Control Room does not continuously shell out
207	  against a process an operator started elsewhere without it being told to.
208	  §2.4 covers how an operator can still see an external session's recent
209	  output on demand.
210	- **Bounded concurrency.** Relay threads are capped at
211	  `CLAUDE_AGENTS_MAX_RELAYS` (default 20); if the owned-session count exceeds
212	  that, the supervisor logs a warning and relays the most-recently-updated
213	  sessions first. This is a real, documented cap, not a silent truncation —
214	  the roster itself (unaffected by the cap) still lists every owned session
215	  regardless of relay status, and a card without an active relay shows
216	  "transcript relay paused (fleet at capacity)" rather than an empty pane
217	  that looks like nothing happened.
218	
219	### 2.4 New read endpoints in `admin/server.py`
220	
221	- `GET /api/claude-agents` — reads `claude_bg:roster` from Redis. If the key
222	  is absent or the JSON fails to parse, returns `{"error":
223	  "supervisor_unavailable", "agents": []}` with a 200 (a rendering concern,
224	  not a hard failure — the fleet section shows a "supervisor not running"
225	  state, the rest of the Control Room is unaffected). Never calls
226	  `list_agents` synchronously — this is a pure Redis read, matching how
227	  `api_matrix` reads its own cached hashes [admin/server.py:384-421].
228	- `GET /api/claude-agents/<id>/logs` — for **external** sessions only (owned
229	  sessions get their transcript via `/api/events/claude_bg_<id>` and don't
230	  need this route); validates `id` against the same `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}$`
231	  pattern from §1.4, calls `claude_agents_client.get_logs(id)` synchronously
232	  with the client's bounded timeout, truncates the response to a fixed cap
233	  (e.g. 64 KB) matching the "bound... log-tail size" constraint, and returns
234	  it as plain text with a note that this is a one-shot, best-effort tail, not
235	  a live stream.
236	- `GET /api/claude-agents/daemon` — calls `daemon_status()` synchronously
237	  (bounded 5s timeout — a single fast status check, not a poll loop, so it
238	  stays inside Flask per §2.1's carve-out) and returns its JSON, or `{
239	  "running": false }` derived from exit code 1. Read-only; no control
240	  affordance is attached to this response, matching acceptance criterion 8.
241	- `GET /api/events/claude_bg_<id>` — no new code. This is the existing
242	  `/api/events/<cell_id>` route [admin/server.py:450-490], invoked with a
243	  `claude_bg_`-prefixed id. Retained-history replay, the `replay_complete`
244	  boundary, and heartbeat pings all behave exactly as they do for any other
245	  cell id, because the supervisor publishes through the same
246	  `LivePublisher`/Redis log+channel primitives every other relay uses
247	  [src/instrument/live.py:47-105].
248	
249	### 2.5 Transcript fidelity — stated honestly
250	
251	Owned-session transcripts are relayed continuously from shortly after launch
252	(§2.3), so in practice they are close to gapless — the same shape of
253	guarantee OpenCode sessions get from `scripts/supervise.py`'s
254	`relay_once`/`_relay_session` [scripts/supervise.py:178-193]. But the
255	underlying primitive is different in kind, not just in polling cadence:
256	`claude logs <id>` is documented as printing "recent output," a bounded
257	tail with no stated retention window, not a durable, gapless history API the
258	way OpenCode's `/api/session/{id}/event` SSE stream is
259	[admin/opencode_client.py:114-137]. Two consequences follow, and both are
260	stated in the UI and in acceptance criterion 4 rather than left implicit:
261	
262	1. There is a small window — bounded by `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL`,
263	   default 10s — between `claude --bg` returning a session id and the
264	   supervisor's first relay poll picking it up. Output produced in that
265	   window is not lost *if* `claude logs` still has it in its tail on the
266	   first poll (very likely at 10s for a session that just started), but this
267	   spec makes no stronger guarantee than that.
268	2. If `claude logs`'s own retention window is ever shorter than expected
269	   (e.g. under sustained high-volume output), lines could be dropped between
270	   two consecutive polls with no way for the Control Room to detect the gap,
271	   because `claude logs` exposes no cursor/offset primitive to detect
272	   under-run against — only content to diff against last-seen text. This is
273	   a limitation of the CLI contract, not an implementation gap; if a future
274	   CLI version adds an offset- or cursor-based tail command, this design
275	   should switch to it.
276	
277	External-session transcripts (§2.4's one-shot `/logs` fetch) carry the same
278	"recent output, not full history" caveat, more visibly so, since there is no
279	continuous relay building a longer retained window at all.
280	
281	## 3. Control path + door discipline
282	
283	### 3.1 Mutation guard
284	
285	Every new `POST` route reuses the loopback + same-origin + JSON +
286	`Idempotency-Key` guard `admin/server.py` already enforces for
287	`/api/design-sessions/*`
288	[admin/server.py:104-124, 127-178] — implemented as a small sibling helper,
289	`_claude_agent_mutation_body()`, with the same checks (loopback remote addr,
290	loopback `Host`, matching `Origin`, `application/json`, size cap, required
291	`Idempotency-Key`) rather than a parameterized shared function, to honor the
292	constraint that `/api/design-sessions*` behavior must not change
293	[docs/scope.md §4]. The existing `_idempotent_design_response` reservation
294	pattern (Redis `SET NX` + replay-on-retry) is reused the same way, under a
295	`claude-agent:<operation>:<id>` cache-key namespace so a retried Stop
296	request can't double-fire.
297	
298	### 3.2 `POST /api/claude-agents` — start
299	
300	Body: `{"workdir": "<allowlist key>", "task": "<string>", "model":
301	"<optional string>", "advisor": "<optional enum>"}`.
302	
303	- `workdir` must be a key in a configured allowlist, `FINOPS_CLAUDE_AGENT_WORKDIRS`
304	  (same `PATH{os.pathsep}PATH...` env shape as
305	  `FINOPS_DESIGN_WORKDIRS` [admin/server.py:85-94], parsed by a small
306	  sibling function rather than by extending `_design_sessions()`, again to
307	  avoid touching the design-session code path). A raw filesystem path from
308	  the browser is never accepted, matching the same rule
309	  `DesignSessionManager` already applies to `workdir_key`
310	  [admin/design_sessions.py:284-288].
311	- `task` is bounded the same way `intent`/`prompt` are for design sessions
312	  (`MAX_DESIGN_PROMPT_CHARS`-equivalent cap).
313	- `model`, if present, is passed through `_resolve_claude_model`
314	  [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:203-211] so a UI-selected model produces
315	  the identical `--model` argument the headless adapter would produce for
316	  the same id.
317	- `advisor`, if present, must be one of a fixed set (`fable`, `opus`,
318	  `sonnet`) or match a full model-id shape; it is passed straight through as
319	  `--advisor <value>` with no other logic, per the scope's constraint.
320	- The launch always includes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, consistent
321	  with every other Claude CLI invocation this framework already makes
322	  headlessly [src/instrument/claude_adapter.py:291-299] — Control-Room-
323	  launched sessions are unattended by construction, the same as headless
324	  runs. Per the CLI reference, this flag persists across a `respawn` for the
325	  life of the session.
326	- On success, the client's `start_agent` result includes the new session id
327	  (parsed from `claude --bg`'s stdout, which the reference states prints the
328	  session id and management commands). The handler adds that id to
329	  `claude_bg:owned_sessions` (Redis `SADD`, no TTL — ownership is permanent
330	  for the id's lifetime; the set is only pruned when `rm` succeeds, §3.4)
331	  before returning `{"ok": true, "id": "<id>"}` to the browser. The next
332	  supervisor poll tick (≤ `CLAUDE_AGENTS_POLL_INTERVAL` seconds later) picks
333	  the session up as owned and starts its relay, per §2.3.
334	
335	### 3.3 `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/stop` and `/respawn`
336	
337	Both require the id to be present in `claude_bg:owned_sessions`; if not,
338	the handler returns `403 {"error": "session not started from the Control
339	Room; manage it with the claude CLI directly"}` **before** shelling out —
340	this is the server-side half of the ownership boundary from §1.2, not just a
341	hidden button.
342	
343	- **Stop** (`claude stop <id>`, `kill` is the CLI's alias for the same
344	  operation, so this feature exposes only `stop`) is a one-way door in the
345	  sense the scope's constraint means: it ends the running process
346	  immediately, and the UI must not let that happen from a stray click. The
347	  frontend requires `window.confirm` before sending the request, matching
348	  the existing Interrupt-confirmation pattern
349	  [admin/static/app.js:1284]. The response states plainly that the
350	  conversation is preserved and can be resumed with **Respawn** — stop is
351	  not "conversation deleted," it is "process ended, resumable."
352	- **Respawn** (`claude respawn <id>`) restarts a running-or-stopped session
353	  with its conversation intact. It is control, not destructive — the scope
354	  explicitly says it "does not require the same confirmation weight, though
355	  it should still be a deliberate click, not a default action." The UI
356	  implements this as a plain button (no `window.confirm`), not bound to any
357	  keyboard shortcut or auto-triggered flow, and the response/roster entry is
358	  checked to confirm the conversation id is unchanged before the card
359	  re-renders as running.
360	
361	### 3.4 `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/rm`
362	
363	Requires ownership (§3.3's same check) and `window.confirm` (rm removes the
364	session from `claude agents`'s own list; while the reference states the
365	transcript stays on disk and remains reachable via `claude --resume`, that
366	resume path is outside this UI, so from the Control Room's perspective this
367	is effectively a one-way door on the *card*, even though the data isn't
368	deleted). On success, the handler also removes the id from
369	`claude_bg:owned_sessions` and its relay cursor key, and the response text
370	states explicitly: "removed from the Claude agents list; transcript remains
371	on disk and is reachable via `claude --resume <id>` outside the Control
372	Room."
373	
374	### 3.5 `POST /api/claude-agents/daemon/stop`
375	
376	The most severe control this feature exposes, because `claude daemon stop`
377	affects **every** session the local `claude daemon` hosts, including
378	external ones this UI has no relationship to and cannot even fully
379	enumerate confidently (an external session could be under a cwd outside the
380	configured allowlist and never appear in this feature's roster at all, yet
381	still be killed by this call). Accordingly:
382	
383	- Body: `{"keep_workers": true}` by default; the operator must pass
384	  `{"keep_workers": false}` explicitly to also end every running session
385	  along with the supervisor. The handler rejects a missing `keep_workers`
386	  field rather than defaulting silently in the request-parsing layer, so the
387	  choice is always explicit in the logged request body, not just the UI
388	  copy.
389	- The frontend requires a `window.confirm` whose copy names the blast
390	  radius plainly, e.g.: *"Stop the Claude agents daemon? This affects every
391	  background session on this machine, not just ones started from the
392	  Control Room."* — and a second, visually distinct confirm/toggle before
393	  `keep_workers: false` can even be sent, so "end every session" cannot be
394	  reached by the same single click that stops the supervisor.
395	- This control lives in the daemon panel (§1.3), never inside a per-session
396	  card and never as part of any bulk/multi-select action.
397	
398	### 3.6 Door-discipline summary
399	
400	| Action | Reversible? | Confirmation | Scope |
401	|---|---|---|---|
402	| Start | n/a (creates) | none (deliberate form submit) | one session, owned workdir only |
403	| Stop/kill | Process ends now; conversation resumable via Respawn | `window.confirm` | one owned session |
404	| Respawn | Fully reversible (that's its purpose) | deliberate click, no confirm dialog | one owned session |
405	| Rm | Removed from list; transcript stays on disk, resumable only outside this UI | `window.confirm` | one owned session |
406	| Daemon stop (keep-workers) | Supervisor restarts and reconnects; sessions survive | `window.confirm`, blast-radius copy | every session on the host |
407	| Daemon stop (end sessions) | Every hosted session ends | `window.confirm` + separate explicit toggle | every session on the host |
408	| Detach | N/A — browser only | none needed | browser tab only, no process effect |

410	## 4. Challenge adjudication
411	
412	Every point in `docs/challenge.md` is addressed below. §0 and §1 of the
413	challenge (CLI-fact verification and five points of agreement) are adopted
414	without modification and are folded into §1–§3 above without a separate
415	row, since there was nothing to resolve. The four disagreement points
416	(§2.1–§2.4) get individual verdicts.
417	
418	| # | Challenge point | Verdict | Why |
419	|---|---|---|---|
420	| 4.1 | **2.1** Unscoped `--all` roster mixes external sessions in with no visual distinction, exposing Stop/Rm on sessions the operator didn't start | **Adopted, with a stronger mechanism than proposed.** Challenge suggested `--cwd`-scoped polling + an owned-set + "strongest confirmation copy (or disable outright)" for external sessions. This spec adopts `--cwd`-scoped polling and the owned-set (§1.2, §2.3), and picks the "disable outright" branch rather than stronger confirmation copy: external sessions get no Stop/Respawn/Rm affordance in the UI *and* the corresponding endpoints reject the action server-side if the id isn't owned (§3.3). Outright disabling is simpler to reason about and audit than a confirmation-copy variant that still has a code path to the destructive action; there's no legitimate Control-Room workflow that needs to stop a session it didn't start. |
421	| 4.2 | **2.2** Relaying only the selected session loses early history a session accumulates before anyone selects its card, unlike OpenCode's gapless relay | **Synthesized.** Full adoption of "relay every roster session continuously" was rejected because, combined with 4.1's ownership split, it would mean continuously polling external sessions the Control Room has no business polling. Instead: owned sessions (the only ones this feature can act on anyway) get continuous relay starting within one poll interval of launch (§2.3), which is close to OpenCode's guarantee for the sessions that matter to this UI; external sessions get on-demand one-shot log fetches only (§2.4), never continuous relay. §2.5 states explicitly, in both this document and acceptance criterion 4, that `claude logs` is a bounded-tail primitive, not the gapless equivalent OpenCode's SSE history gives — exactly the honesty check the challenge asked for, without over-building continuous relay for sessions this UI shouldn't be polling in the first place. |
422	| 4.3 | **2.3** Embedding polling threads + subprocess calls in the single-process Flask dev server risks the exact resource pressure its own docstring warns about | **Adopted.** `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py` (§2.1, §2.3) takes over all polling and relay subprocess calls, structurally parallel to `scripts/supervise.py`. `admin/server.py` only reads Redis for `GET /api/claude-agents` and the transcript route. Short, bounded, one-shot mutating commands (start/stop/respawn/rm/daemon status/daemon stop) stay as synchronous Flask-side subprocess calls, per the challenge's own carve-out — it is the *polling* that doesn't belong in the request-serving process, not all subprocess use. |
423	| 4.4 | **2.4** The Problem section motivates this feature by naming both the observe/control half and the AI-flagging half of `scripts/supervise.py`, but only the first is built, unstated | **Adopted.** §1.1 states explicitly that AI health-flagging for Claude background sessions is out of scope for this phase and is a real, buildable follow-on once this phase's `claude logs` relay exists to feed it (the challenge's own observation that `supervise_once`'s batching already knows how to summarize this shape of text). This is the "add one sentence to §3/§4" resolution the challenge offered as sufficient, applied here instead as an explicit phase-scope statement. |

425	## 5. Acceptance criteria
426	
427	1. `admin/claude_agents_client.py` wraps `claude agents --json --all --cwd
428	   <path>`, `claude --bg`, `claude logs <id>`, `claude stop <id>`, `claude
429	   respawn <id>`, `claude rm <id>`, `claude daemon status`, and `claude
430	   daemon stop --any [--keep-workers]` as subprocess calls (stdin closed on
431	   every call), each returning parsed JSON/text or a distinguishable error
432	   for a missing binary, non-zero exit, malformed JSON, or timeout.
433	2. `scripts/claude_agents_supervisor.py` runs as a separate process; it is
434	   the only thing that polls `claude agents --json --all` or `claude logs`.
435	   It writes `claude_bg:roster` (TTL'd, tagged `owned`) and relays log lines
436	   for owned, non-terminal-or-recently-terminal sessions only, into
437	   `LivePublisher(f"claude_bg_{id}")`, capped at `CLAUDE_AGENTS_MAX_RELAYS`
438	   concurrent relay threads with the overflow surfaced in the UI, not
439	   silently dropped.
440	3. `GET /api/claude-agents` reads `claude_bg:roster` from Redis and never
441	   blocks on a live CLI call; a missing/stale key returns a
442	   `supervisor_unavailable` state instead of hanging or 500ing.
443	4. A background session's transcript is exposed through the existing `GET
444	   /api/events/<cell_id>` endpoint under `claude_bg_<id>`; the
445	   `replay_complete` boundary and retained-history behavior are unchanged
446	   for both pre-existing and new cell ids; both the UI copy and this spec
447	   state that Claude transcripts are best-effort/tail-bounded relays of a
448	   "recent output" primitive, not a gapless history API.
449	5. `POST /api/claude-agents` starts a session via `claude --bg`, accepts
450	   only a workdir key from `FINOPS_CLAUDE_AGENT_WORKDIRS` (never a raw
451	   path), resolves the model through `_resolve_claude_model`, accepts an
452	   optional fixed-set `advisor` value, enforces the loopback/JSON/
453	   Idempotency-Key guard, records the new id in `claude_bg:owned_sessions`,
454	   and returns the new session id.
455	6. `POST /api/claude-agents/<id>/stop`, `/respawn`, and `/rm` each: reject
456	   (403, before any subprocess call) an id absent from
457	   `claude_bg:owned_sessions`; enforce the mutation guard; and for stop/rm,
458	   require that the client went through an explicit confirmation step.
459	   Respawn's response/roster reflects an unchanged conversation id. Rm's
460	   response states plainly that the transcript remains on disk.
461	7. `GET /api/claude-agents/daemon` returns `claude daemon status` output (or
462	   a derived "supervisor not running" state from exit code 1) as a read-only
463	   observation with no control affordance attached.

1	"""Small native-v2 HTTP client for portal-owned OpenCode sessions.
2	
3	The Control Room backend uses raw HTTP because it is already a Python process;
4	adding a Node SDK bridge would create another service and expose no additional
5	API guarantees.  The browser never receives the OpenCode server address.
6	"""
7	
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import json
11	from collections.abc import Iterator
12	from dataclasses import dataclass
13	from typing import Any
14	from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
15	from urllib.parse import quote, urlencode
16	from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
17	
18	MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES = 2_000_000
19	MAX_SSE_EVENT_BYTES = 2_000_000
20	
21	
22	def _model_ref(model: str) -> dict[str, str]:
23	    """Translate a flat ``"provider/model"`` id into the native Model.Ref shape."""
24	    provider, _, mid = model.partition("/")
25	    return {"providerID": provider, "id": mid}
26	
27	
28	@dataclass
29	class OpenCodeError(RuntimeError):
30	    """Actionable failure returned by or encountered while calling OpenCode."""
31	
32	    message: str
33	    status: int = 502
34	
35	    def __str__(self) -> str:
36	        return self.message
37	
38	
39	class OpenCodeClient:
40	    """Call the native OpenCode v2 session and durable-event endpoints."""
41	
42	    def __init__(self, base_url: str, *, timeout: float = 15.0) -> None:
43	        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip("/")
44	        self.timeout = timeout
45	
46	    def _json_request(
47	        self,
48	        method: str,
49	        path: str,
50	        body: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
51	        *,
52	        allow_empty: bool = False,
53	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
54	        """Issue one bounded JSON request and reject malformed success bodies."""
55	        payload = json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None
56	        headers = {"Accept": "application/json"}
57	        if payload is not None:
58	            headers["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
59	        request = Request(f"{self.base_url}{path}", data=payload, headers=headers, method=method)
60	        try:
61	            with urlopen(request, timeout=self.timeout) as response:  # noqa: S310 - configured loopback service
62	                raw = response.read(MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES + 1)
63	        except HTTPError as error:
64	            detail = error.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
65	            raise OpenCodeError(
66	                f"OpenCode rejected the request ({error.code}): {detail or error.reason}",
67	                error.code,
68	            ) from error
69	        except (URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:
70	            raise OpenCodeError(f"OpenCode is unavailable: {error}") from error
71	
72	        if len(raw) > MAX_HTTP_BODY_BYTES:
73	            raise OpenCodeError("OpenCode JSON response exceeded the 2000000-byte limit")
74	        if allow_empty and not raw.strip():
75	            return {}
76	        try:
77	            result = json.loads(raw)
78	        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
79	            raise OpenCodeError("OpenCode returned malformed JSON") from error
80	        if not isinstance(result, dict):
81	            raise OpenCodeError("OpenCode returned an unexpected JSON response")
82	        return result
83	
84	    def create_session(self, *, location: str | dict[str, Any], model: str | dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
85	        """Create a native session bound to an approved repository location.
86	
87	        Accepts flat ``"provider/model"`` and directory-path strings and translates
88	        them to the native structured refs (Model.Ref / LocationRef).
89	        """
90	        loc = location if isinstance(location, dict) else {"directory": location}
91	        mod = model if isinstance(model, dict) else _model_ref(model)
92	        return self._json_request("POST", "/api/session", {"location": loc, "model": mod})
93	
94	    def send_input(self, session_id: str, prompt: str | dict[str, Any], *, delivery: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
95	        """Queue or steer one durable prompt into an existing native session."""
96	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
97	        body = prompt if isinstance(prompt, dict) else {"text": prompt}
98	        return self._json_request(
99	            "POST",
100	            f"/api/session/{encoded}/prompt",
101	            {"prompt": body, "delivery": delivery},
102	        )
103	
104	    def interrupt(self, session_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
105	        """Request interruption of active work without detaching the browser."""
106	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
107	        return self._json_request("POST", f"/api/session/{encoded}/interrupt", {}, allow_empty=True)
108	
109	    def messages(self, session_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
110	        """Return the native projected message history for explicit recovery."""
111	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
112	        return self._json_request("GET", f"/api/session/{encoded}/message")
113	
114	    def iter_events(self, session_id: str, *, after: str | None = None) -> Iterator[dict[str, Any]]:
115	        """Yield JSON objects from one native durable SSE subscription.
116	
117	        SSE ``id`` is retained as ``_sse_id`` when the JSON body does not carry
118	        an aggregate sequence.  Multi-line data fields are joined according to
119	        the SSE framing rules, while comments and unknown fields are ignored.
120	        """
121	        encoded = quote(session_id, safe="")
122	        query = f"?{urlencode({'after': after})}" if after else ""
123	        request = Request(
124	            f"{self.base_url}/api/session/{encoded}/event{query}",
125	            headers={"Accept": "text/event-stream"},
126	            method="GET",
127	        )
128	        try:
129	            response = urlopen(request, timeout=max(self.timeout, 65.0))  # noqa: S310 - configured service
130	        except HTTPError as error:
131	            detail = error.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
132	            raise OpenCodeError(
133	                f"OpenCode event stream failed ({error.code}): {detail or error.reason}",
134	                error.code,
135	            ) from error
136	        except (URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:
137	            raise OpenCodeError(f"OpenCode event stream is unavailable: {error}") from error
138	
139	        content_type = response.headers.get_content_type()
140	        if content_type != "text/event-stream":
141	            response.close()
142	            raise OpenCodeError(f"OpenCode event stream returned {content_type}, not text/event-stream")
143	
144	        data_lines: list[str] = []
145	        data_size = 0
146	        event_id: str | None = None
147	        try:
148	            for raw_line in response:
149	                line = raw_line.decode("utf-8", errors="replace").rstrip("\r\n")
150	                if line == "":
151	                    if data_lines:
152	                        raw_data = "\n".join(data_lines)
153	                        try:
154	                            event = json.loads(raw_data)
155	                        except json.JSONDecodeError:
156	                            event = {"type": "raw", "data": raw_data}
157	                        if not isinstance(event, dict):
158	                            event = {"type": "raw", "data": event}
159	                        if event_id and not any(key in event for key in ("sequence", "aggregateSequence")):
160	                            event["_sse_id"] = event_id
161	                        yield event
162	                    data_lines = []
163	                    data_size = 0
164	                    event_id = None
165	                    continue
166	                if line.startswith(":"):
167	                    continue
168	                field, _, value = line.partition(":")
169	                value = value[1:] if value.startswith(" ") else value
170	                if field == "data":
171	                    data_lines.append(value)
172	                    data_size += len(value.encode(errors="replace"))
173	                    if data_size > MAX_SSE_EVENT_BYTES:
174	                        raise OpenCodeError("OpenCode SSE event exceeded the 2000000-byte limit")
175	                elif field == "id":
176	                    event_id = value
177	        finally:
178	            response.close()
179

127	def _idempotent_design_response(
128	    operation: str, body: dict, action
129	) -> tuple[Response, int] | Response:
130	    """Reserve and replay one JSON mutation result using Redis atomic ``SET NX``."""
131	    supplied_key = request.headers["Idempotency-Key"]
132	    request_digest = hashlib.sha256(
133	        json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
134	    ).hexdigest()
135	    cache_id = hashlib.sha256(f"{operation}\0{supplied_key}".encode()).hexdigest()
136	    cache_key = f"control_room:idempotency:{cache_id}"
137	    reservation = json.dumps({"state": "pending", "request_digest": request_digest})
138	    try:
139	        redis_client = _redis()
140	        reserved = redis_client.set(
141	            cache_key,
142	            reservation,
143	            nx=True,
144	            ex=IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS,
145	        )
146	        if not reserved:
147	            existing_raw = redis_client.get(cache_key)
148	            existing = json.loads(existing_raw) if existing_raw else {}
149	            if existing.get("request_digest") != request_digest:
150	                return (
151	                    jsonify({"error": "Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request"}),
152	                    409,
153	                )
154	            if existing.get("state") == "complete":
155	                return jsonify(existing.get("body", {})), int(existing.get("status", 200))
156	            return (
157	                jsonify({"error": "matching mutation is still in progress", "retryable": True}),
158	                409,
159	            )
160	    except Exception as error:
161	        return jsonify({"error": f"idempotency store unavailable: {error}"}), 503
162	
163	    try:
164	        response = make_response(action())
165	    except Exception as error:
166	        response = make_response(_design_error(error))
167	    completed = json.dumps({
168	        "state": "complete",
169	        "request_digest": request_digest,
170	        "status": response.status_code,
171	        "body": response.get_json(silent=True) or {},
172	    })
173	    with suppress(Exception):
174	        redis_client.set(cache_key, completed, ex=IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS)
175	    # The action already completed. A cache-write failure must not invite a
176	    # new-key retry that duplicates paid or filesystem-changing work.
177	    return response

293	        "output_tokens": output_tokens,
294	        "reasoning_tokens": reasoning_tokens,

300	def _retained_telemetry(redis_client, cell_ids) -> dict[str, Any]:
301	    """Build an additive retained-window snapshot from existing event logs.
302	
303	    Each log is independently optional. A transient per-cell read failure does
304	    not erase the baseline matrix response; ``available`` records that the
305	    telemetry extension is incomplete while the legacy status data remains
306	    usable.
307	
308	    All log reads are issued in a single non-transactional pipeline so the
309	    fleet snapshot costs one round trip, not one per cell.
310	    """
311	    cells = {}
312	    total_cost = 0.0
313	    input_tokens = 0.0
314	    output_tokens = 0.0
315	    cost_samples = input_samples = output_samples = 0
316	    available = True
317	    capped = False
318	
319	    keys = [f"{EVENT_LOG_PREFIX}{cell_id}" for cell_id in cell_ids]
320	    try:
321	        pipe = redis_client.pipeline(transaction=False)
322	        for key in keys:
323	            pipe.lrange(key, 0, -1)
324	        histories = pipe.execute()
325	    except Exception:
326	        # A connection-level failure marks telemetry incomplete but must not
327	        # erase the legacy matrix response (same contract as today).
328	        histories = [None] * len(cell_ids)
329	
330	    for cell_id, history in zip(cell_ids, histories):
331	        if history is None:
332	            available = False
333	            history = []
334	        capped = capped or len(history) >= EVENT_LOG_MAX
335	
336	        samples = []

451	def api_events(cell_id) -> Response:
452	    """Replay retained cell events, mark the boundary, then stream live data.
453	
454	    The named boundary is additive: clients listening through ``onmessage``
455	    continue to receive the same raw event frames, while Control Room clients
456	    can exclude replay from the rolling burn-rate window.
457	    """
458	    log_key = f"{EVENT_LOG_PREFIX}{cell_id}"
459	    channel = f"{EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX}{cell_id}"
460	
461	    def gen():
462	        r = _redis()
463	        # Subscribe before reading history so an event published during replay
464	        # is queued by Redis instead of falling through the history/live gap.
465	        pubsub = r.pubsub()
466	        pubsub.subscribe(channel)
467	        try:
468	            history = r.lrange(log_key, 0, -1)
469	            for payload in reversed(history):
470	                yield f"data: {payload}\n\n"
471	        except Exception:
472	            pass
473	        yield f"event: replay_complete\ndata: {json.dumps({'cell_id': cell_id})}\n\n"
474	        last_beat = time.time()
475	        try:
476	            while True:
477	                msg = pubsub.get_message(ignore_subscribe_messages=True, timeout=1.0)
478	                if msg:
479	                    yield f"data: {msg['data']}\n\n"
480	                elif time.time() - last_beat >= HEARTBEAT_SECONDS:
481	                    yield ": ping\n\n"
482	                    last_beat = time.time()
483	        finally:
484	            try:
485	                pubsub.unsubscribe(channel)
486	                pubsub.close()
487	            except Exception:
488	                pass

490	    return _sse(gen())

121	    def __init__(

123	        *,
124	        root: Path,
125	        redis_factory: Callable[[], Any],
126	        opencode: OpenCodeClient,
127	        workdirs: dict[str, Path],
128	        start_relays: bool = True,

132	        self.opencode = opencode

134	        self.start_relays = start_relays
135	        self.draft_dir = Path(tempfile.gettempdir()) / "dynamic-code-control-room-drafts"

140	        """Expose labels, not arbitrary server filesystem paths, to the browser."""
141	        return [{"key": key, "label": path.name or key} for key, path in self.workdirs.items()]

143	    def _load_all(self) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
144	        """Read only portal-owned metadata from its dedicated Redis hash."""
145	        raw = self.redis_factory().hgetall(DESIGN_SESSIONS_KEY)
146	        sessions: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
147	        for portal_id, payload in raw.items():
148	            try:
149	                value = json.loads(payload)
150	            except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
151	                continue
152	            if isinstance(value, dict) and value.get("portal_id") == portal_id:
153	                sessions[portal_id] = value
154	        return sessions

156	    def _load(self, portal_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
157	        """Load one owned session or raise a route-friendly missing error."""
158	        payload = self.redis_factory().hget(DESIGN_SESSIONS_KEY, portal_id)
159	        if payload is None:
160	            raise KeyError(portal_id)
161	        try:
162	            session = json.loads(payload)
163	        except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as error:
164	            raise RuntimeError("design session metadata is unreadable") from error
165	        if not isinstance(session, dict) or session.get("portal_id") != portal_id:
166	            raise RuntimeError("design session ownership metadata is invalid")
167	        return session

169	    def _store(self, session: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
170	        """Persist one complete metadata snapshot to avoid split-field reads."""
171	        self.redis_factory().hset(
172	            DESIGN_SESSIONS_KEY,
173	            session["portal_id"],
174	            json.dumps(session, separators=(",", ":")),
175	        )

178	        """Merge fields into the latest snapshot to avoid stale-object erasure."""
179	        with self._lock:

181	            latest.update(values)

185	    def _write_spec_atomic(self, destination: Path, content: str, *, overwrite: bool) -> bool:
186	        """Write in the destination directory, atomically preserving no-replace."""
187	        descriptor, temporary_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=f".{destination.name}.", dir=destination.parent)
188	        try:
189	            with os.fdopen(descriptor, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
190	                handle.write(content)
191	                handle.flush()
192	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
193	            if overwrite:
194	                os.replace(temporary_name, destination)
195	            else:
196	                try:
197	                    # Hard-link creation is atomic and refuses an existing name;
198	                    # unlinking the private temporary name leaves the new file.
199	                    os.link(temporary_name, destination)
200	                except FileExistsError:
201	                    return False
202	                os.unlink(temporary_name)
203	            return True
204	        finally:
205	            with suppress(FileNotFoundError):
206	                os.unlink(temporary_name)

234	        sessions.sort(

236	                item.get("lifecycle_state") not in {"active", "drafting"},
237	                str(item.get("updated_at", "")),
238	            ),
239	            reverse=False,
240	        )
241	        # ISO timestamps sort lexically; reverse each lifecycle group explicitly.
242	        active = [item for item in sessions if item.get("lifecycle_state") in {"active", "drafting"}]
243	        inactive = [item for item in sessions if item not in active]
244	        active.sort(key=lambda item: str(item.get("updated_at", "")), reverse=True)
245	        inactive.sort(key=lambda item: str(item.get("updated_at", "")), reverse=True)
246	        ordered = active + inactive
247	        if self.start_relays:
248	            for item in ordered:
249	                if item.get("opencode_session_id") and item.get("lifecycle_state") not in {"unavailable"}:
250	                    self._ensure_relay(item["portal_id"])
251	        return {"sessions": [self._public(item) for item in ordered], "workdirs": self.approved_workdirs()}

342	    def _publish(self, session: dict[str, Any], event: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
343	        """Publish once into the existing bounded Redis transcript transport."""
344	        payload = json.dumps(event, separators=(",", ":"), default=str)

351	    def _ensure_relay(self, portal_id: str) -> None:
352	        """Start at most one daemon relay per session in this Flask process."""
353	        with self._lock:
354	            existing = self._relay_threads.get(portal_id)
355	            if existing and existing.is_alive():
356	                return
357	            thread = threading.Thread(target=self._relay, args=(portal_id,), daemon=True, name=f"design-{portal_id}")
358	            self._relay_threads[portal_id] = thread
359	            thread.start()

361	    def _relay(self, portal_id: str) -> None:
362	        """Reconnect native SSE with durable sequence tracking and bounded backoff."""
363	        backoff = 1.0
364	        while True:
365	            try:
366	                relayed = self._relay_once(portal_id)
367	                if relayed:
368	                    backoff = 1.0
369	                else:
370	                    # A clean but empty disconnect should not create a busy loop.
371	                    time.sleep(backoff)
372	                    backoff = min(backoff * 2, 15.0)
373	            except Exception as error:  # Relay failure must not kill the Flask process.
374	                try:
375	                    session = self._load(portal_id)
376	                    session["lifecycle_state"] = "reconnecting"
377	                    session["relay_error"] = str(error)[:500]
378	                    session["updated_at"] = _utc_now()
379	                    self._store(session)
380	                    self._publish(session, {"type": "relay_error", "message": str(error), "sessionID": session.get("opencode_session_id")})
381	                except Exception:
382	                    return
383	                time.sleep(backoff)
384	                backoff = min(backoff * 2, 15.0)

386	    def _relay_once(self, portal_id: str) -> int:
387	        """Relay one native SSE connection and return the published event count.
388	
389	        Keeping a single connection pass separate makes durable replay behavior
390	        deterministic under tests while the daemon wrapper owns reconnect delay.
391	        """
392	        session = self._load(portal_id)
393	        native_id = session.get("opencode_session_id")
394	        if not native_id:
395	            return 0
396	        relayed = 0
397	        for event in self.opencode.iter_events(native_id, after=session.get("last_sequence")):
398	            sequence = _event_sequence(event)
399	            # Aggregate sequences are unique.  Do not republish the event that
400	            # ended the previous connection if the server replays it.
401	            if sequence and sequence == session.get("last_sequence"):
402	                continue
403	            self._publish(session, normalize_native_event(event, native_id))
404	            if sequence:
405	                session["last_sequence"] = sequence
406	            session = self._update_metadata(
407	                portal_id,
408	                last_sequence=session.get("last_sequence"),
409	                lifecycle_state="active",
410	                updated_at=_utc_now(),
411	            )
412	            relayed += 1
413	        return relayed

437	    def draft_state(self, portal_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
438	        """Read one coherent draft snapshot and apply authoritative validation."""
439	        session = self._load(portal_id)
440	        path = Path(session["draft_path"])
441	        validated_at = _utc_now()
442	        base: dict[str, Any] = {
443	            "session_id": portal_id,
444	            "revision": session.get("revision", 0),
445	            "draft_state": "no_draft",
446	            "yaml": "",
447	            "validation": {"valid": False, "errors": [], "validated_at": validated_at},
448	            "matrix": None,
449	            "saved": None,
450	            "capabilities": {"save": False, "run": False, "enqueue": False, "reason": None},
451	        }
452	        try:
453	            file_stat = path.lstat()
454	        except FileNotFoundError:
455	            base["capabilities"]["reason"] = "Waiting for the agent to write the assigned draft"
456	            return base
457	        except OSError as error:
458	            base["draft_state"] = "unavailable"
459	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [f"Draft could not be inspected: {error}"]
460	            base["capabilities"]["reason"] = "Draft state unavailable"
461	            return base
462	        if stat.S_ISLNK(file_stat.st_mode) or not stat.S_ISREG(file_stat.st_mode):
463	            base["draft_state"] = "unavailable"
464	            base["validation"]["errors"] = ["Assigned draft must be a regular file, not a symlink"]
465	            base["capabilities"]["reason"] = "Draft state unavailable"
466	            return base
467	        if file_stat.st_size > MAX_DRAFT_BYTES:
468	            base["draft_state"] = "invalid_yaml"
469	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [f"Draft exceeds the {MAX_DRAFT_BYTES}-byte limit"]
470	            return base
471	        try:
472	            flags = os.O_RDONLY | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0)
473	            with os.fdopen(os.open(path, flags), "rb") as handle:
474	                raw = handle.read(MAX_DRAFT_BYTES + 1)
475	        except OSError as error:
476	            base["draft_state"] = "unavailable"
477	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [f"Draft could not be read: {error}"]
478	            base["capabilities"]["reason"] = "Draft state unavailable"
479	            return base
480	        if len(raw) > MAX_DRAFT_BYTES:
481	            base["draft_state"] = "invalid_yaml"
482	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [f"Draft exceeds the {MAX_DRAFT_BYTES}-byte limit"]
483	            return base
484	        text = raw.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
485	        digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
486	        with self._lock:
487	            # Polling requests can overlap.  Compare against the latest digest
488	            # while assigning the monotonic revision.
489	            session = self._load(portal_id)
490	            if digest != session.get("draft_digest"):
491	                session["revision"] = int(session.get("revision", 0)) + 1
492	                session["draft_digest"] = digest
493	                session["updated_at"] = validated_at
494	        base["revision"] = session["revision"]
495	        base["yaml"] = text
496	
497	        try:
498	            document = yaml.safe_load(text)
499	        except yaml.YAMLError as error:
500	            base["draft_state"] = "invalid_yaml"
501	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [str(error)]
502	            self._update_draft_metadata(session, base)
503	            return base
504	        try:
505	            if not isinstance(document, dict):
506	                raise ValueError("ExperimentSpec YAML root must be a mapping")
507	            spec = ExperimentSpec.from_dict(document)
508	        except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError) as error:
509	            base["draft_state"] = "construction_error"
510	            base["validation"]["errors"] = [str(error)]
511	            self._update_draft_metadata(session, base)
512	            return base
513	
514	        errors = validate_spec(spec)
515	        # Session kind is an artifact constraint, not a replacement for the
516	        # ExperimentSpec validator.  It is evaluated only after validate_spec.
517	        if not SAFE_SPEC_ID.fullmatch(str(spec.name)):
518	            errors = [*errors, "spec.name must contain only letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens"]
519	        if session["kind"] == "workflow" and spec.workflow.kind != "agent_task":
520	            errors = [*errors, "workflow design requires workflow.kind 'agent_task'"]
521	        if session["kind"] == "workflow":
522	            phases = spec.workflow.params.get("phases") if isinstance(spec.workflow.params, dict) else None
523	            if not isinstance(phases, list) or not phases or not all(
524	                isinstance(phase, dict) and phase.get("name") and phase.get("kind") for phase in phases
525	            ):
526	                errors = [*errors, "workflow design requires a non-empty workflow.params.phases list"]
527	        if session["kind"] == "experiment":
528	            if not spec.rules:
529	                errors = [*errors, "experiment design requires at least one rule"]
530	            if not spec.metrics:
531	                errors = [*errors, "experiment design requires at least one metric"]
532	            if spec.comparison is None:
533	                errors = [*errors, "experiment design requires a comparison"]
534	        base["validation"]["errors"] = errors
535	        if errors:
536	            base["draft_state"] = "validation_errors"
537	            self._update_draft_metadata(session, base)
538	            return base
539	
540	        base["draft_state"] = "valid"
541	        base["validation"]["valid"] = True
542	        base["capabilities"]["save"] = True
543	        if session["kind"] == "experiment":
544	            active_levels = [len(factor.levels) for factor in spec.factors if factor.active]
545	            cardinality = math.prod(active_levels) if active_levels else 1
546	            if cardinality > MAX_MATRIX_CELLS:
547	                base["matrix"] = {"count": cardinality, "preview": [], "truncated": True}
548	                base["capabilities"]["reason"] = (
549	                    f"Matrix has {cardinality} cells, above the {MAX_MATRIX_CELLS}-cell preview cap"
550	                )
551	            else:
552	                try:
553	                    cells = experiment_matrix(spec)
554	                except Exception as error:
555	                    base["capabilities"]["reason"] = f"Matrix preview failed: {error}"
556	                    cells = None
557	            if cardinality <= MAX_MATRIX_CELLS and cells is not None:
558	                cell_ids = [cell.get("cell_id") for cell in cells]
559	                reason = None
560	                if not cells:
561	                    reason = "Valid spec produced zero cells"
562	                elif len(set(cell_ids)) != len(cell_ids):
563	                    reason = "Valid spec produced duplicate cell IDs"
564	                elif len(cells) > MAX_MATRIX_CELLS:
565	                    reason = f"Matrix has {len(cells)} cells, above the {MAX_MATRIX_CELLS}-cell preview cap"
566	                base["matrix"] = {
567	                    "count": len(cells),
568	                    "preview": cells[:MATRIX_PREVIEW_CELLS],
569	                    "truncated": len(cells) > MATRIX_PREVIEW_CELLS,
570	                }
571	                base["capabilities"]["reason"] = reason or "Validated; enqueue unavailable (no generic dispatcher)"
572	
573	        if session.get("saved_revision") == session["revision"] and session.get("saved_path"):
574	            base["saved"] = {"revision": session["saved_revision"], "path": session["saved_path"]}
575	            if session["kind"] == "workflow":
576	                base["capabilities"]["run"] = True
577	        self._update_draft_metadata(session, base)
578	        return base

584	            draft_state=state["draft_state"],

586	            revision=session.get("revision", 0),

590	    def save(self, portal_id: str, *, filename: str, overwrite: bool) -> dict[str, Any]:
591	        """Revalidate and atomically persist a safe repository-relative spec."""
592	        if not SAFE_SPEC_NAME.fullmatch(filename) or Path(filename).name != filename:
593	            raise ValueError("filename must be a safe .yaml or .yml basename")
594	        state = self.draft_state(portal_id)
595	        if not state["validation"]["valid"]:
596	            raise ValueError("draft is not valid")
597	        # ``draft_state`` validated this exact coherent snapshot.  Using the
598	        # returned text prevents an agent write between validation and save.
599	        content = state["yaml"]
600	        destination_dir = (self.root / "experiments" / "specs").resolve()
601	        destination_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
602	        destination = destination_dir / filename
603	        if destination.is_symlink():
604	            raise ValueError("destination symlinks are not allowed")
605	        if destination.parent.resolve() != destination_dir:
606	            raise ValueError("destination escapes experiments/specs")
607	        if destination.exists() and not overwrite:
608	            return {
609	                "ok": False,
610	                "conflict": True,
611	                "path": destination.relative_to(self.root).as_posix(),
612	                "message": "Spec already exists; explicit overwrite confirmation is required",
613	            }
614	
615	        if not self._write_spec_atomic(destination, content, overwrite=overwrite):
616	            return {
617	                "ok": False,
618	                "conflict": True,
619	                "path": destination.relative_to(self.root).as_posix(),
620	                "message": "Spec already exists; explicit overwrite confirmation is required",
621	            }
622	
623	        relative = destination.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()
624	        self._update_metadata(
625	            portal_id,
626	            saved_path=relative,
627	            saved_revision=state["revision"],
628	            saved_digest=hashlib.sha256(content.encode()).hexdigest(),
629	            updated_at=_utc_now(),
630	        )
631	        return {"ok": True, "path": relative, "revision": state["revision"], "content": content}

633	    def run_workflow(
634	        self,
635	        portal_id: str,
636	        *,
637	        goal: str,
638	        model: str,
639	        workdir_key: str,
640	        timeout: int,
641	        commit: bool,
642	        backend: str | None = None,
643	        thinking_budget_tokens: int = 0,
644	        output_token_limit: int = 0,
645	    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
646	        """Launch the existing workflow CLI under a separate fleet identity."""
647	        session = self._load(portal_id)
648	        if session["kind"] != "workflow":
649	            raise ValueError("only workflow design sessions can run")
650	        state = self.draft_state(portal_id)
651	        if not state["capabilities"]["run"] or not state.get("saved"):
652	            raise ValueError("workflow must be valid and saved at the current revision")
653	        saved_candidate = self.root / state["saved"]["path"]
654	        if saved_candidate.is_symlink():
655	            raise ValueError("saved workflow artifact is unavailable or unsafe")
656	        saved_path = saved_candidate.resolve()
657	        specs_root = (self.root / "experiments" / "specs").resolve()
658	        if saved_path.parent != specs_root or not saved_path.is_file():
659	            raise ValueError("saved workflow artifact is unavailable or unsafe")
660	        saved_bytes = saved_path.read_bytes()
661	        if hashlib.sha256(saved_bytes).hexdigest() != session.get("saved_digest"):
662	            raise ValueError("saved workflow changed after Save; save the current revision again")
663	        try:
664	            saved_document = yaml.safe_load(saved_bytes)
665	            if not isinstance(saved_document, dict):
666	                raise ValueError("saved ExperimentSpec YAML root must be a mapping")
667	            saved_spec = ExperimentSpec.from_dict(saved_document)
668	        except (yaml.YAMLError, TypeError, ValueError, KeyError) as error:
669	            raise ValueError(f"saved workflow is invalid: {error}") from error
670	        saved_errors = validate_spec(saved_spec)
671	        if saved_errors or saved_spec.workflow.kind != "agent_task":
672	            detail = saved_errors or ["workflow.kind must be 'agent_task'"]
673	            raise ValueError(f"saved workflow failed validation: {detail}")
674	        if not goal.strip() or not model.strip():
675	            raise ValueError("goal and model are required")
676	        workdir = self.workdirs.get(workdir_key)
677	        if workdir is None:
678	            raise ValueError("workdir is not approved")
679	        if not isinstance(timeout, int) or isinstance(timeout, bool) or not 1 <= timeout <= 7200:
680	            raise ValueError("timeout must be between 1 and 7200 seconds")
681	        if backend not in {None, "", "opencode", "claude_cli"}:
682	            raise ValueError("backend must be opencode or claude_cli")
683	        budgets = {
684	            "thinking_budget_tokens": thinking_budget_tokens,
685	            "output_token_limit": output_token_limit,
686	        }
687	        for name, value in budgets.items():
688	            if not isinstance(value, int) or isinstance(value, bool) or not 0 <= value <= 2_000_000:
689	                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be an integer between 0 and 2000000")
690	
691	        execution_id = f"workflow_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}"
692	        command = [
693	            sys.executable,
694	            "scripts/run_workflow.py",
695	            "--spec",
696	            state["saved"]["path"],
697	            "--goal",
698	            goal.strip(),
699	            "--model",
700	            model.strip(),
701	            "--workdir",
702	            str(workdir),
703	            "--timeout",
704	            str(timeout),
705	            "--thinking-budget-tokens",
706	            str(thinking_budget_tokens),
707	            "--output-token-limit",
708	            str(output_token_limit),
709	        ]
710	        if backend:
711	            command.extend(["--backend", backend])
712	        if not commit:
713	            command.append("--no-commit")
714	
715	        redis_client = self.redis_factory()
716	        redis_client.hset(STATUS_KEY, execution_id, "queued")
717	        redis_client.publish(STATUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps({"cell_id": execution_id, "status": "queued"}))
718	        thread = threading.Thread(
719	            target=self._run_process,
720	            args=(execution_id, command),
721	            daemon=True,
722	            name=execution_id,
723	        )
724	        thread.start()
725	        return {
726	            "ok": True,
727	            "execution_id": execution_id,
728	            "stream_id": execution_id,
729	            "launch": {
730	                "spec": state["saved"]["path"],
731	                "goal": goal.strip(),
732	                "model": model.strip(),
733	                "workdir": workdir_key,
734	                "timeout": timeout,
735	                "backend": backend or "auto",
736	                "thinking_budget_tokens": thinking_budget_tokens,
737	                "output_token_limit": output_token_limit,
738	                "commit": commit,
739	            },

1	"""Live telemetry — Redis Pub/Sub publisher for background experiment progress.
2	
3	No-ops gracefully when Redis is unavailable or ``FINOPS_CELL_ID`` is unset, so
4	an experiment run never fails because the dashboard is down. Channels mirror
5	``scripts/monitor.py``:
6	
7	    - status hash:      ``story_status``         (cell_id -> queued|running|done|failed|timeout)
8	    - pub/sub channel:  ``status``               (status transitions)
9	    - pub/sub channel:  ``events:{cell_id}``     (per-cell session event stream)
10	"""
11	
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import json
15	import os
16	from typing import Any
17	
18	REDIS_HOST = os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_HOST", "127.0.0.1")
19	REDIS_PORT = int(os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_PORT", "6380"))
20	REDIS_DB = int(os.environ.get("FINOPS_REDIS_DB", "1"))
21	STATUS_KEY = "story_status"
22	STATUS_CHANNEL = "status"
23	EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX = "events:"
24	EVENT_LOG_PREFIX = "events_log:"
25	EVENT_LOG_MAX = 500
26	
27	
28	def _connect() -> Any:
29	    """Connect to Redis, returning None if unavailable (never raises)."""
30	    try:
31	        import redis
32	
33	        r = redis.Redis(
34	            host=REDIS_HOST,
35	            port=REDIS_PORT,
36	            db=REDIS_DB,
37	            decode_responses=True,
38	            socket_connect_timeout=2,
39	            socket_keepalive=False,
40	        )
41	        r.ping()
42	        return r
43	    except Exception:
44	        return None
45	
46	
47	class LivePublisher:
48	    """Publish live experiment progress to Redis Pub/Sub.
49	
50	    Disables itself permanently after the first failure so a downed Redis
51	    server costs one attempt, not one per event.
52	    """
53	
54	    def __init__(self, cell_id: str | None = None) -> None:
55	        self.cell_id = cell_id or os.environ.get("FINOPS_CELL_ID", "").strip()
56	        self._r = _connect() if self.cell_id else None
57	        self._disabled = self._r is None
58	
59	    @property
60	    def enabled(self) -> bool:
61	        return not self._disabled and bool(self.cell_id)
62	
63	    def publish_status(self, status: str) -> None:
64	        """Publish a cell status transition to the ``status`` channel."""
65	        if not self.enabled:
66	            return
67	        try:
68	            self._r.publish(STATUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps({"cell_id": self.cell_id, "status": status}))
69	        except Exception:
70	            self._disabled = True
71	
72	    def set_status(self, status: str) -> None:
73	        """Record status in the ``story_status`` hash AND publish the transition.
74	
75	        The portal's fleet reads the hash (``GET /api/matrix``); the live stream reads
76	        the channel (``GET /api/status``). Both must be updated for a cell to appear.
77	        """
78	        if not self.enabled:
79	            return
80	        try:
81	            self._r.hset(STATUS_KEY, self.cell_id, status)
82	            self._r.publish(STATUS_CHANNEL, json.dumps({"cell_id": self.cell_id, "status": status}))
83	        except Exception:
84	            self._disabled = True
85	
86	    def publish_event(self, event: dict[str, Any] | str) -> None:
87	        """Publish a single session event to ``events:{cell_id}``.
88	
89	        Also appends to a bounded history list (``events_log:{cell_id}``) so a
90	        portal can replay the tail before subscribing — Redis pub/sub has no
91	        message history.
92	        """
93	        if not self.enabled:
94	            return
95	        payload = event if isinstance(event, str) else json.dumps(event)
96	        channel = f"{EVENT_CHANNEL_PREFIX}{self.cell_id}"
97	        log_key = f"{EVENT_LOG_PREFIX}{self.cell_id}"
98	        try:
99	            # Persist before publishing so "delivered live" implies "already
100	            # retained": a poll that starts after a publish is guaranteed to
101	            # observe the entry (or it was evicted from the shared bounded
102	            # window, which the fleet flag labels). The reverse failure mode
103	            # (lpush succeeds, publish fails) degrades to a bounded poll pickup.
104	            self._r.lpush(log_key, payload)
105	            self._r.ltrim(log_key, 0, EVENT_LOG_MAX - 1)
106	            self._r.publish(channel, payload)
107	        except Exception:
108	            self._disabled = True
109	
110	
111	def make_publisher() -> LivePublisher | None:
112	    """Return a LivePublisher for the current cell, or None if disabled.
113	
114	    Driven by the ``FINOPS_CELL_ID`` env var (set by the experiment worker so
115	    every backend session in the process tree publishes to the right cell).
116	    """
117	    cell_id = os.environ.get("FINOPS_CELL_ID", "").strip()
118	    if not cell_id:
119	        return None
120	    return LivePublisher(cell_id)

"""Claude CLI adapter — run Claude Code headless and emit opencode-format JSONL.

Anthropic's ToS prohibits using Claude Pro/Max subscriptions inside opencode's
provider layer. This module sidesteps that by driving the official ``claude``
CLI directly (``--output-format stream-json``) and translating its event
stream into opencode's ``run --format json`` event schema, so every downstream
parser (``analyze_trajectories``, ``efficiency``, lab books) works unchanged.

Translation is stateful: Claude splits a tool call into an ``assistant``
``tool_use`` block (running) and a ``user`` ``tool_result`` block (done), while
opencode emits a single completed ``tool_use`` event. ``ClaudeStreamAdapter``
buffers pending calls and flushes one event per completed tool.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import time
from collections.abc import Callable
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

    """Map Claude CLI ``result.usage`` to opencode's ``step-finish`` tokens.

    Claude does not break out reasoning tokens in usage (thinking is folded
    into ``output_tokens``), so ``reasoning`` is always 0 — matching the
    framework's honest-token semantics. Cache fields map directly.
    """
    if not isinstance(usage, dict):
        usage = {}
    input_tokens = int(usage.get("input_tokens", 0) or 0)
    output_tokens = int(usage.get("output_tokens", 0) or 0)
    cache_read = int(usage.get("cache_read_input_tokens", 0) or 0)
---
    # Claude 4.5 generation (still available):

def _resolve_claude_model(model: str) -> str:
    """Map an opencode-style model id to a Claude Code ``--model`` value."""
    model_id = (model.split("/", 1)[1] if "/" in model else model).strip()
    if not model_id or model_id.lower() == "anthropic":
        return ""
    key = model_id.lower()
    if key in _CLAUDE_MODEL_ALIASES:
        return _CLAUDE_MODEL_ALIASES[key]
    return model_id


def _claude_model_arg(model: str) -> list[str]:
    """Derive a ``--model`` argument from an opencode-style ``provider/model`` id."""
    resolved = _resolve_claude_model(model)

        return []
    return ["--model", resolved]


def _estimate_claude_cost(result: AgenticResult, model: str) -> float:

    from .efficiency import get_pricing

    pricing = get_pricing("anthropic", model)
    return (
        result.prompt_tokens * pricing["input"]
        + result.completion_tokens * pricing["output"]
        + result.reasoning_tokens * pricing.get("reasoning", pricing["output"])
        + result.cache_read_tokens * pricing["cache_read"]
        + result.cache_write_tokens * pricing["cache_write"]

546	   * short, bounded tail avoids suppressing legitimate identical future events.

814	  /** Drop overlays once a matrix request started after they were observed. */
815	  function pruneReconciledSamples(snapshotRequestSequence) {
816	    for (const [cellId, samples] of state.liveSamplesByCell.entries()) {
817	      // Samples arriving during this request remain until the next snapshot,
818	      // because the current Redis read may have happened before their publish.

821	      )

827	  /** Merge newer status-stream transitions over a potentially older snapshot. */
828	  function applyStatusOverrides(snapshotCells) {
829	    const cells = { ...snapshotCells }
830	    for (const [cellId, override] of state.statusOverrides.entries()) {
831	      if (core.normalizeStatus(cells[cellId]) === core.normalizeStatus(override.status)) {
832	        state.statusOverrides.delete(cellId)
833	        continue
834	      }
835	      if (override.remainingSnapshots > 0) {
836	        cells[cellId] = override.status
837	        override.remainingSnapshots -= 1
838	      } else {
839	        // Repeated matrix disagreement wins if the status stream missed a later transition.
840	        state.statusOverrides.delete(cellId)
841	      }
842	    }
843	    return cells
